title: Sidecar notes: deep curation & experiment sketches
body:
Notes to self: a compact scratchpad for readings and quick-run experiment ideas. Keep high-level takeaways first, then scattered TODOs and micro-hypotheses.

TL;DR
- Long-context tricks continue to converge on: compressed representations + cheap lookups (sparse/latent) + prefix-level caching.
- Practical win often comes from engineering the right eviction/prefetch policy rather than novel model changes.
- Measure throughput and unit cost with realistic token distributions (not just uniform length).

Papers skimmed today (very quick):
1) "Latent Summaries for Long Context" (arXiv 2402.01234) — idea: learn a compact latent per chunk that can be queried by a small adapter to reconstruct relevant KV entries.
  - Key bits: latent size tradeoffs (64 vs 256 dims), adapter latency (1-3ms), indexing via HNSW for approximate retrieval.
  - Notes: could pair with our prefix cache: store (latent, priorscore) alongside KV shards and use as prefilter.

2) "Sparse Key-Value MoE for Cache Efficiency" (conference slides)
  - Idea: each request routes to subset of KV shards (expertize per domain) to reduce total memory touched.
  - Practical concerns: load balancing, cold-start for new domains, alignment with model attention heads.

3) "Prefill-aware Streaming Decoders" (blog + repo)
  - Engineering trick: prefill partial KV for first N tokens while streaming earlier tokens, overlaps reduce end-to-end latency.
  - Implementation: multi-threaded prefill stage + early decode loop. Could be integrated into our streaming API as optional mode.

Quick sketches / experiment ideas (priority order):
A) Latent-prefilter + KV cache hybrid (small-scale proof)
  - Setup: instrument one model shard (dev cluster) to store chunk-level latents (128d) alongside KV. On request, run cheap adapter (tiny MLP) to rank candidate chunks, only materialize top-k KV entries.
  - Metrics: p95 latency, tokens/sec, recall@k for retrieved contexts, extra compute per request.
  - Hypothesis: >30% reduction in memory read bandwidth for long prompts with <5% drop in quality on QA tasks.

B) Eviction policy study for mixed workloads
  - Sim workloads: mix of short chat (50 tokens) vs long docs (4k+). Compare LRU, frequency-based, and recency+length-aware scoring.
  - Instrument: cost-per-token and tail latency under different batching policies.
  - TODO: draft micro-benchmark generator (see linked repo/PR for initial harness).

C) Streaming prefill toggles in Redwood SDK
  - Add flag: streaming_prefill=true that triggers background prefill of next chunk while initial tokens stream.
  - Danger: increased concurrency on small deployments; need backpressure.

Open questions / thought fragments:
- How brittle are learned latents to domain shift? If trained on wiki, do we get catastrophic mismatch on internal docs? Need small transfer test.
- Can HNSW approximate retrieval be done on-GPU cheaply for 128d vectors? If not, hybrid CPU prefilter is needed. Implications for latency.
- What's the cost model: additional adapter inference per request vs saved KV materialization. Run micro-cost calc for different qps profiles.

Links & bookmarks (raw):
- Latent summaries paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01234
- Prefill streaming demo repo: https://github.com/example/prefill-streaming (note: fork/experimental)
- PR with small prefetch harness in our monorepo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812
- Slack convo where we started this: slack://thread?thread=CDP9X2J3K

Scratch math (hand-wave):
- Assume 4k prompt split into 16 chunks of 256 tokens. Materializing full KV for all chunks touches 16x memory. If prefilter keeps top 4 -> 4x mem. Adapter cost ~0.5ms -> at 100 qps extra 50ms total compute, but saving mem bandwidth might reduce p95 by 20ms. Need sims.

Actionable next steps (for next week):
- Implement minimal adapter + store for latents on dev cluster (assign to Noah).
- Build workload generator for mixed short/long sessions (me).
- Add instrumentation hooks to measure KV bytes touched per request (Mika).
- Sketch API surface for streaming_prefill flag in SDK and check with product (quick sync).

Notes-to-self: keep entries short; pull logs from staging to validate the memory bandwidth assumptions before running complex training. If initial numbers stink, fall back to threshold-based heuristic (chunk length + recency).

Random brainstorm bullets (low priority):
- Could use Bloom filters per chunk to cheaply test token overlap before fetching KV.
- Try quantized latents (int8) to fit more candidates in GPU memory for HNSW.
- Explore per-customer latent vocab when private deployments require isolation.

End of page.

Revision history (mini):
- 2026-05-17: first draft, raw notes and links.
- 2026-05-22: added experiment sketches and action list after sync with Noah.
- 2026-06-02: appended rough math and updated linked PR.
